headline: Neighbors trust the repairs. Google is showing two listings for the same shop.
summary: JM Appliance Repair is a Spring Valley appliance repair service that comes to the house, and its Nextdoor story describes more than 15 years of hands-on work with brands like LG, Samsung and Whirlpool. Neighbors named it a Nextdoor Neighborhood Favorite in 2025, and a neighbor was recommending it by name in the summer of 2025, which is the kind of word of mouth a small repair business lives on. The basics are in good shape on the service-area Google listing: it is open, the name is JM Appliance Repair LLC in normal capitalization, the phone number (619) 536-7937 matches Nextdoor, there are 10 photos added by the business and 9 reviews, and the hours are Monday through Friday 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM and Saturday 8:00 AM to 1:30 PM. The biggest leftover is that Google is also showing a second card for the same shop, with different hours, photos, reviews and website fields, which can split how you show up. The service-area listing is the more complete one to keep, and we can help sort out the extra card. A few smaller touches would help too: the website listed on your Nextdoor page, jm-appliance.com, isn't loading, so the straightforward fix is to take that link off; the service-area Google card lists jmappliancerepair.com, but that address also doesn't currently load a shop page, so if that domain is yours, point it at a real page or take it off the card until it works; and both Google cards still use a general service category instead of appliance repair.

signals.note: Your service-area Google listing is live and marked open, so people searching for appliance repair around Spring Valley can find you on Maps. There is also a second Google card for the same shop, and both cards still use a general service category, so Google has less to go on when deciding which searches to show you for.
signals.next: Use the service-area Google listing as the main one, and set its primary category to Appliance repair service, plus any close secondary ones that fit, like Washer and dryer repair service. Then check that the service area covers the towns you actually drive to. We can help sort out the extra card.

signals.note: Your number, (619) 536-7937, is the same on both Google cards and on Nextdoor, so a caller lands in the right place whichever one they find first. That's the door that matters most for a repair business, and it's working.
signals.next: Use (619) 536-7937 exactly as-is on any new website or listing. If you add a text-friendly line later, list it as an extra number rather than replacing this one.

signals.note: The two Google cards do not agree on hours. The service-area listing shows Monday through Friday 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM and Saturday 8:00 AM to 1:30 PM, while the other card starts weekdays earlier and is closed Saturday, so a customer who goes by the wrong card may call at a time you aren't taking jobs.
signals.next: Pick the hours you really keep, including whether you take Saturday jobs, and put the same hours on the service-area Google listing and on Nextdoor. If you do emergency or after-hours calls, say so in one short line on both.

signals.note: Your service-area Google listing already has 10 photos, all added by JM Appliance Repair LLC. The other Google card still has only one photo, posted by a customer, which is another reason the service-area listing is the one to keep.
signals.next: Keep those photos on the service-area listing you stay with. Adding a new one every month or two keeps the listing looking active.

signals.note: The website listed on your Nextdoor page, jm-appliance.com, isn't loading, so anyone who taps it hits a dead end. The straightforward fix is to take that link off Nextdoor. Your service-area Google card lists jmappliancerepair.com, but that address also doesn't currently load a shop page.
signals.next: Remove the jm-appliance.com link from Nextdoor. If you own jmappliancerepair.com, point it at a real page or take it off the Google card until it works.

signals.note: Your name, phone and town line up, but Google is currently showing two cards for the same shop, with different hours, photos, reviews and website fields. Neither website URL is loading a shop page right now, and having two listings can split how you show up.
signals.next: Keep the service-area Google listing, and we can help merge or remove the extra card. Once you have a working website, use the same link, or no link, on Google and Nextdoor.
